haiku-low.q1: It signs in normally. The linked sub goes straight to start_session, with no password or email comparison. The stored email is never changed.
haiku-low.q2: The user must enter that account's password on the confirm page. A correct password inserts the google_identities row, sets email_verified_at if NULL, then calls start_session.
haiku-low.q3: Each wrong password adds one to failed_logins and the pending link is kept. The fifth wrong password sets a 15-minute lock, resets failed_logins, deletes the pending link, and shows an incorrect password message.
haiku-low.q4: With no matching user, a user with no password and a verified email is created, linked, and signed in. If email_verified is false, sign-in is refused, nothing is created, and the user is told to use email and password.
haiku-low.q5: Both fail with the error page 'sign-in link invalid or expired'. The flow expires after 600 s or is consumed by the first GETDEL, so nothing changes and the existing session is kept.
haiku-low.q6: start_session(user_id) creates a new sessions row and sets a new sid cookie. The old sid row is deleted if the browser sent one.
haiku-low.q7: Neither a password nor an email match is required, only a live session for the flow user. If that sub belongs to another user, it is refused. If this user already has a different Google account, it is refused until unlinked.
haiku-low.q8: In Redis under goidc:<state> for 600 s, with the state also in the goidc_state cookie. GETDEL removes the flow at the first callback whatever the outcome, or the TTL does.
haiku-low.q9: In Redis under glink:<token> for 600 s, holding sub, user_id and next. The glink cookie holds the token. Success, Cancel, lock or TTL deletes it; a wrong password keeps it.
haiku-low.q10: In Postgres table google_identities. Its sub PRIMARY KEY gives one user per Google account, and its unique user_id gives one Google account per user, both enforced by the database.
haiku-low.q11: The user sees 'Google sign-in failed, try again'. Nothing is created and no pending link is made. The code is not retried, so the user must start a new flow.
haiku-low.q12: The flow's intent (login or settings) selects the callback path. For settings, the flow stores user_id, and the sid cookie must map to a live session whose user_id matches it.

sonnet.q1: Nothing changes. Accounts are matched only by `sub`, never email, so the linked `sub` goes straight to start_session (after the lock check). A Google email change never removes the link.
sonnet.q2: The user must prove the account's password. A pending link (glink, 600 s) is created and the confirm page asks for the password. Only if the bcrypt check passes is the google_identities row inserted and start_session called. (Also the user must not already have another Google account, and email_verified must be true.)
sonnet.q3: Each wrong password adds 1 to failed_logins and the pending link is kept, with the form shown again. On the fifth, locked_until is set to now plus 15 min, failed_logins reset to 0, the pending link deleted, and the user goes to the login page with an incorrect password message. The next Google attempt meets the lock at confirm.
sonnet.q4: Verified email with no matching user: create a user (lowercased email, NULL password_hash, email_verified_at now) and the google_identities row in one transaction, then sign in via start_session. If email_verified is false: refuse, login page says Google email not verified, use email and password; nothing created.
sonnet.q5: Both fail the same way. The flow expires after 600 s (and is consumed by GETDEL on first callback), so an expired or reused state gives an error page: sign-in link invalid or expired. Nothing changes and any existing session is kept.
sonnet.q6: The same ordinary session as a password login, via start_session(user_id): no new session type. It deletes the old sid row if one was sent, inserts a new sessions row, sets the sid cookie, and redirects to next (if relative) or /home.
sonnet.q7: Neither a password nor an email match is required (email is not compared and stored email never changes). The user must be signed in, with the sid matching the flow's user_id. If the sub already belongs to another user, it is refused (back to settings) and nothing changes; if it is already linked to this user, it reports already linked.
sonnet.q8: In the Redis flow record goidc:<state> (state, nonce, PKCE verifier, intent, user_id for settings, origin page, next), with the state also in the goidc_state cookie. Removed by GETDEL at the first callback whatever the outcome, or by the 600 s TTL. The cookie is cleared on the callback response or expires.
sonnet.q9: In Redis key glink:<token> (TTL 600 s) holding sub, user_id and next. The browser refers to it by the glink cookie holding the token. It is deleted on success, Cancel, lock (fifth wrong password, or locked at confirm), or TTL expiry; a wrong password keeps it. The cookie is cleared with it.
sonnet.q10: In the new Postgres table google_identities (sub, user_id, linked_at). The primary key on sub gives one user per Google account, and the UNIQUE user_id gives one Google account per user. The database enforces both, so races show up as unique violations. user_id cascades on user delete.
sonnet.q11: The user sees an error page: Google sign-in failed, try again. Nothing is created and there is no pending link. The code is not retried; the user must start a new flow.
sonnet.q12: By the intent stored in the flow record (login or settings). For settings, the flow records the signed-in user's user_id at start, and at callback the sid cookie must map to a live, unexpired sessions row whose user_id equals the flow's user_id. Otherwise an error page appears and nothing is linked.
